dossier_meta.statement_text: Problem Is there an eighth triangle free strongly regular graph?
dossier_meta.context_text: A regular graph $ G $ is strongly regular if there exist integers $ \lambda, \mu $ so that every pair of adjacent vertices have exactly $ \lambda $ common neighbors, and every pair of nonadjacent vertices have exactly $ \mu $ common neighbors. To eliminate degeneracies, we shall further assume that $ \mu \ge 1 $ . If $ G $ is $ k $ -regular and $ |V(G)| = n $ , then we say that $ G $ is a $ (n,k,\lambda,\mu) $ strongly regular graph. There are exactly seven triangle-free strongly regular graphs known: The five cycle, the Petersen Graph , The Clebsch Graph, the Hoffman-Singleton Graph , The Gewirtz Graph, the Higman-Sims Graph, and a $ (77,16,0,4) $ strongly regular subgraph of the Higman-Sims graph. Every Moore Graph of diameter 2 is a triangle-free strongly regular graph, so if there is a 57-regular Moore Graph of diameter 2, this would add another to the list. See Andries Brouwer's graph descriptions for more on these graphs.
